style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: A handheld thermal camera lying on a painted-wood windowsill in a hallway, beside a cold window frame at dusk, its small screen glowing with a false-color heat map of that same window — amber and rust blooms over slate blue. 100mm macro, razor-sharp focal plane on the glowing screen, shallow depth of field, the graphite body and pale hallway wall falling soft behind. Cold blue dusk light enters from the window at left; the screen's warm glow answers from the right. Palette: bone white, graphite, rust amber. Dust on the sill, fine film grain, no people, no legible text, no logos. Extreme asymmetry: camera low on the right third, generous negative space to the left.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, unreadable numbers on screen, watermark, logo
rationale: The story turns on one physical, purchasable thing — the $109 camera — whose price and whose epistemic limit are both the news, so a 100mm macro with razor focus on the glowing false-color screen states the thesis in one glance. The windowsill setting keeps the photograph inside the home-diagnostics world the article serves, and the amber heat map against cold blue dusk dramatizes pattern-versus-verdict without a single word. Macro is reserved here precisely because the protagonist is a handable device, not a systemic facility.
subject: a handheld thermal camera on a hallway windowsill, its screen glowing with a false-color heat map of the window beside it
core_thesis: A thermal camera cheap enough to be a holiday stocking stuffer now sits in homeowners' hands the same month a lab proved an infrared image can be deliberately staged and the camera maker's own guide admitted the picture is a pattern, not a verdict.
core_conflict: Democratized cheap thermal imaging versus the epistemic limits of the image itself — the camera nominates a cold spot, but only a second tool convicts, and the picture cannot even score its own repairs.
composition: Extreme asymmetry: the camera sits low on the right third of the sill, the window frame and pale wall falling into soft negative space on the left.
